$comment: Accepted-for-this-release defects. A waiver here does NOT hide a failure:
the rule still runs, still reports FAIL, and meets_the_bar still prints it —
it just stops that one rule blocking an unrelated release. This exists so a
known defect in one app cannot hold every other app's work hostage, which is
what happens when shared-file changes pull every app into the push range.
RULES FOR THIS FILE:
- Every entry names ONE app and ONE rule (waivers) or ONE finding
(acceptedFindings: title + citation). No wildcards, no 'all'.
- Every entry states why it is accepted and what will fix it.
- `since` is the date it was first accepted. An entry that keeps being
renewed is a decision to look at, not a fact of life.
- lg-shipped is NOT waivable. Ship proof is the one thing a release cannot
take on credit; enforced in code, not by convention.
acceptedFindings (F5 independent judge-diff):
- Each entry names ONE app, ONE finding (title + citation), the reviewed
commit, a date, and why it is accepted for this release.
- independentReviewOk is true only when the report exists, is complete,
is pinned to the app's newest SOURCE commit, AND every failing finding
is individually listed here at that commit.
- A missing/stale/incomplete report still fails regardless of this list.
- An entry whose commit does not match the current review does not apply.
- Blankets, wildcards, and 'all' are rejected in code and never match.

waivers.reason: Sub-44px chips on /examples. Pre-existing, found before this release and deliberately left alone: the page is being rebuilt under task #43 and hacking CSS into a page about to be replaced is waste.

Measured: 'no text search input with accessible name matching /search|find/i on the collection view'. The /examples collection genuinely has no search control. It is a real feature gap, not a measurement artifact, and it lands with the task #43 rebuild of that page rather than as a control bolted onto a page about to be replaced.

Measured: 'app has queryable domain data but no assistant endpoint (expected functions/api/assistant.ts or similar under functions/api/)'. app-builder has no assistant at all; adding one is a feature, not a fix, and it has not been scoped.
waivers.fixedBy: unscheduled — needs a product decision on whether app-builder wants an assistant

waivers.reason: Measured: 'no <link rel="canonical"> found — home must declare an absolute canonical URL'. Small and genuinely fixable; deferred only because it is being taken with the rest of the SEO pass rather than alone.

Measured: SOURCES.md, INTEGRATIONS.md and COMPETITORS.md are all absent, so the prior-art step (R23/R29/R31) did not run for this app. Writing those honestly means actually doing the prior-art research, which is real work and cannot be faked into a file to clear a rule.
waivers.fixedBy: next release — run the prior-art skill against app-builder

waivers.reason: Measured on public/favicon-96.png: ink coverage 100.0% (>92%, a solid blob) and worst tab contrast 0.018 (<0.05, vanishes against one tab colour). The mark needs regenerating, which is a Grok Imagine job queued with the brand pass.
waivers.fixedBy: next release — regenerate the favicon via the brand-logo skill

waivers.reason: Measured: 'image outside an asset directory: design-refs/design-options/option-1-story-stack-dark-1280.png'. These are design-option reference frames, which proc-design-options requires to exist and hyg-no-binaries objects to. The two rules disagree about the same files; resolving that is a rule question, not an app fix, and it should not be settled in a rush before a push.
waivers.fixedBy: next release — decide whether design-refs is an allowlisted asset path

waivers.reason: Measured: 'duplicated code across src/components/examples/ExampleCard.tsx and src/components/examples/ExampleStory.tsx'. Both components are on /examples and are being replaced by the task #43 rebuild, so extracting a shared component now would be work thrown away.

Measured: '/api/__definitely_absent_<nonce>: status 200 with SPA shell body'. Pages answers unmatched paths with index.html at 200, so an absent /api/* route looks alive. This is a real defect and the most substantive one waived here; it is deferred rather than rushed because the fix is a routing change that deserves its own verification pass.
waivers.fixedBy: next release — add an /api/* 404 handler and re-run the probe

waivers.reason: Measured: 'payments: copy denies it ("does not process payments") but code shows src/i18n/en.ts: "Stripe"'. Needs a read of whether the app truly touches payments or the string is incidental copy in a generated PRD template. Waived to be checked properly rather than guessed at, because a legal claim is the wrong place to guess.
waivers.fixedBy: next release — confirm the payments claim against the code and correct whichever side is wrong

waivers.reason: Measured: 4 evidence problems, all citing app-builder/functions/lib/auth.ts, which is not on disk. Judge verdicts point at a file that does not exist, so the verdicts are stale rather than the code being wrong. Clearing it means re-judging app-builder against its real tree.
waivers.fixedBy: next release — re-judge app-builder, do not re-stamp
